role.en: traveller

bio.en: Moroccan who travelled some 120,000 km over 30 years, from West Africa to China, recording it all in his Rihla.

role.en: humanist poet

bio.en: Father of humanism whose sonnets to Laura set the model for European love poetry for centuries.

role.en: founder of the Muromachi shogunate who turned on Go-Daigo

bio.en: A general who first helped Go-Daigo topple Kamakura, then rebelled against him in 1336 and enthroned a Northern Court emperor. In 1338 he was named shogun and founded the second shogunate, based in Kyoto.

role.en: king who began the Hundred Years' War and won at Crécy

bio.en: Reigned for 50 years. In 1337 he claimed the French throne and started the Hundred Years' War; his archers routed the French at Crécy in 1346. He founded the Order of the Garter, and the Black Death struck during his reign.

role.en: saint and abbot

bio.en: Founder of the Trinity Monastery and Russia's most revered saint, said to have blessed Dmitry Donskoy before Kulikovo.

role.en: emperor who made Prague an imperial capital and issued the Golden Bull

bio.en: King of Bohemia of the Luxembourg dynasty. He founded Prague University (1348), the New Town and the Charles Bridge, built Karlštejn Castle, and with the Golden Bull of 1356 fixed the election of the emperor by seven electors for four centuries.

role.en: grand prince "of all Rus" who died of the plague

bio.en: Eldest son of Ivan Kalita. He tightened Moscow's hold over the other princes, earning the nickname "the Proud", and styled himself grand prince "of all Rus". He died with his sons in the Black Death.

role.en: king captured by the English at Poitiers

bio.en: Captured by the Black Prince at Poitiers in 1356; the franc was first minted to pay his ransom. When the son left as a hostage escaped, the king returned to captivity himself and died in London.

role.en: Persian poet

bio.en: Master of the ghazal and Persian poetry's greatest lyricist; Iranians still consult his Divan for divination.

role.en: sultan who took Adrianople and fell at Kosovo

bio.en: The first to take the title of sultan, he conquered Adrianople (Edirne) and made it his capital and created the Janissary corps. He was killed at the Battle of Kosovo in 1389, by tradition at the hand of the Serbian knight Miloš Obilić.

role.en: grand prince of Moscow, father of Dmitry Donskoy

bio.en: Son of Ivan Kalita who succeeded his brother Simeon after the plague. He ruled cautiously and peacefully, relying on Metropolitan Alexius, who after his death became guardian of the young Dmitry Donskoy.

role.en: second Ashikaga shogun, who held Kyoto against the Southern Court

bio.en: Takauji's son, shogun 1358–1367. He spent his rule fighting the Southern Court and rebel vassals, losing and retaking Kyoto several times, yet handed his son a stable shogunate.

role.en: historian and thinker

bio.en: Author of the Muqaddimah, explaining the rise and fall of states; considered a forerunner of sociology and economics.

role.en: emir and conqueror

bio.en: Conqueror who built an empire from Anatolia to India centred on Samarkand, crushing the Golden Horde and the Ottomans.

role.en: king who regained most of what was lost in the Hundred Years’ War

bio.en: With Constable Bertrand du Guesclin he avoided pitched battles and won back most of the lands lost to England. He began the Bastille and gathered the royal library in the Louvre.

role.en: poet, author of The Canterbury Tales

bio.en: The 'father of English poetry', whose Canterbury Tales established English as a literary language.

role.en: Grand Prince of Moscow

bio.en: Grand Prince who defeated Mamai's army at Kulikovo in 1380; he built Moscow's first white-stone Kremlin.

role.en: Elector Palatine chosen to replace the deposed Wenceslaus

bio.en: Count palatine of the Rhine, elected king in 1400. His 1401–1402 Italian campaign against Gian Galeazzo Visconti of Milan failed, he never won the imperial crown and ruled from Heidelberg.

role.en: shogun who reunited the two imperial courts and built Kinkaku-ji

bio.en: Shogun from 1368; in 1392 he ended the split between the Northern and Southern Courts. He formally retired in 1394 but ruled until his death, opened trade with Ming China by accepting the title 'King of Japan', and built the Golden Pavilion.

role.en: icon painter

bio.en: Russia's greatest icon painter, creator of the Trinity, who decorated cathedrals in Moscow and Vladimir.

role.en: sultan defeated and captured by Timur at Ankara

bio.en: He crushed the crusaders at Nicopolis in 1396 and besieged Constantinople for years, but in 1402 was defeated by Timur at Ankara and died in captivity, plunging the state into a decade of civil war.

role.en: Bohemian king deposed by the electors as "idle and useless"

bio.en: Son of Charles IV. In 1400 the electors stripped him of the German crown for neglect; in Bohemia his reign saw the death of John of Nepomuk (1393), the Decree of Kutná Hora favouring Jan Hus (1409) and the outbreak of the Hussite Wars, amid which he died.

role.en: writer

bio.en: Europe's first known professional woman writer, who defended women's dignity in The Book of the City of Ladies.

role.en: boy king who faced down the Peasants' Revolt and was deposed by his cousin

bio.en: Came to the throne at ten; at fourteen he personally faced Wat Tyler's rebels in the Peasants' Revolt of 1381. His autocratic rule alienated the nobles: in 1399 his cousin Henry Bolingbroke deposed him, and he soon died in captivity at Pontefract Castle.

role.en: first Lancastrian king, who seized the throne from Richard II

bio.en: Henry Bolingbroke, son of John of Gaunt, deposed his cousin Richard II in 1399 and founded the House of Lancaster. He spent his reign putting down revolts — the Percys in the north and Owain Glyndŵr in Wales.

role.en: mad king who named the king of England his heir

bio.en: From 1392 he suffered bouts of madness while the Armagnacs and Burgundians fought for power. After the rout at Agincourt (1415) he signed the Treaty of Troyes, disinheriting his son in favour of Henry V.

role.en: emperor of the Council of Constance that ended the Schism and burned Hus

bio.en: King of Hungary from 1387, defeated by the Turks at Nicopolis (1396). He convened the Council of Constance, which ended the Great Schism, but let Jan Hus be burned despite his safe-conduct — and then spent fifteen years fighting the Hussites.

role.en: church reformer

bio.en: Czech preacher who attacked church corruption; his burning as a heretic at Constance sparked the Hussite Wars.

role.en: admiral and explorer

bio.en: Ming eunuch admiral who led seven huge treasure fleets to India, Arabia and East Africa.

role.en: grand prince who annexed Nizhny Novgorod

bio.en: Son of Dmitry Donskoy and the first grand prince to inherit power by his father's will. He annexed the Nizhny Novgorod principality; in 1395 Timur turned back before reaching Moscow.

role.en: victor of Agincourt who became heir to the French crown

bio.en: He renewed the Hundred Years' War and in 1415 crushed a much larger French army at Agincourt. Under the Treaty of Troyes in 1420 he married Catherine of Valois and was recognised as heir to the French king, but he died at 35.

role.en: shogun who broke off tributary trade with Ming China

bio.en: Shogun from 1394, ruling in his own right after his father's death in 1408. He rejected the demeaning 'King of Japan' title and cut off trade with the Ming in 1411; Korea raided Tsushima during his rule (1419).

role.en: sultan who reunited the realm after Timur

bio.en: The youngest son of Bayezid I, he defeated his brothers in the civil war of 1402–1413 and restored the unity of the Ottoman state; he built the Green Mosque in Bursa.

role.en: ruler and astronomer

bio.en: Timur's grandson who built an observatory in Samarkand and compiled the most accurate star catalogue of his age.

role.en: shogun chosen by lot and murdered by his own vassal

bio.en: A former monk picked in 1428 by drawing lots among Yoshimochi's brothers. He ruled harshly, crushed the rebel Kamakura governor Ashikaga Mochiuji in 1439, and was killed at a banquet by Akamatsu Mitsusuke in 1441 (the Kakitsu Incident).

role.en: King of Joseon Korea

bio.en: Joseon king under whom the Korean alphabet, Hangul, was created; a great patron of science and invention.

role.en: first Habsburg to unite Austria, Bohemia and Hungary

bio.en: Duke of Austria and son-in-law of Sigismund, he inherited the crowns of Hungary and Bohemia and was elected German king in 1438. From him on the Habsburgs held the imperial throne without a break, but he ruled under two years, dying of dysentery on campaign against the Turks.

role.en: inventor of the printing press

bio.en: Invented movable-type printing in Europe and printed the Bible around 1455, transforming the world.

role.en: ruler of Texcoco, poet

bio.en: Poet-king of Texcoco and co-founder of the Aztec Triple Alliance, renowned for his aqueducts and dikes.

role.en: king under whom the Hundred Years’ War ended

bio.en: Thanks to Joan of Arc he was crowned at Reims in 1429. He created the first standing army and by 1453 had driven the English from all of France except Calais.

role.en: sultan who crushed the crusaders at Varna

bio.en: In 1444 he abdicated in favour of the 12-year-old Mehmed II but returned to rout the crusaders at Varna; in 1448 he again defeated John Hunyadi at Kosovo.

role.en: young shogun who died two years after taking office

bio.en: He became shogun in 1423 at 16, but real power stayed with his father Yoshimochi. He died in 1425, reputedly from drink, leaving no heir, and the shogunate went four years without a shogun.

role.en: heroine of the Hundred Years' War

bio.en: A peasant girl who lifted the siege of Orléans and led the Dauphin to his coronation; burned at the stake by the English.

role.en: last emperor crowned in Rome, who reigned for 53 years

bio.en: The longest-reigning emperor. In 1452 he became the last emperor crowned in Rome; he lived through the loss of Vienna to Matthias Corvinus, and by marrying his son Maximilian to Mary of Burgundy laid the foundations of Habsburg world power.

role.en: grand prince blinded in a dynastic civil war

bio.en: He spent a quarter of a century fighting for the throne against his uncle Yury and his sons; in 1446 he was blinded by Dmitry Shemyaka but regained power. Under him the Russian Church became autocephalous in 1448.

role.en: Sapa Inca

bio.en: Transformed the kingdom of Cusco into the Inca Empire; Machu Picchu is believed to have been built for him.

role.en: weak king under whom England lost the Hundred Years' War

bio.en: Became king at nine months old and was the only English king also crowned in Paris. Under him England lost nearly all its French lands and the Wars of the Roses began; he founded Eton College and was killed in the Tower in 1471.

role.en: the "universal spider" who pieced France together

bio.en: Through intrigue and money he overcame rebellious nobles and Charles the Bold of Burgundy. After Charles was killed he annexed the duchy of Burgundy and Picardy, and later Anjou and Provence.

role.en: Ottoman sultan

bio.en: The sultan who captured Constantinople in 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire; known as the Conqueror.

role.en: child shogun who died at the age of nine

bio.en: Son of the murdered Yoshinori, proclaimed shogun in 1442 at the age of eight while the deputy Hosokawa Mochiyuki governed for him. He died the following year, reputedly after a fall from his horse.

role.en: shogun of the Ōnin War and the Silver Pavilion

bio.en: Shogun 1449–1473. The quarrel over whether his brother or his son would succeed him became the Ōnin War (1467–1477), which ruined Kyoto and opened the Sengoku era, while he withdrew into the arts: the tea ceremony and Higashiyama culture flourished and he built Ginkaku-ji.

role.en: Grand Prince of Moscow

bio.en: 'Gatherer of the Russian lands' who annexed Novgorod, ended Horde overlordship in 1480 and rebuilt the Kremlin.

role.en: first Yorkist king, victor in the Wars of the Roses

bio.en: After defeating the Lancastrians at Towton in 1461 he became the first Yorkist king; deposed in 1470, he returned and beat his enemies at Barnet and Tewkesbury. He was a patron of William Caxton, England's first printer.

role.en: Emperor of Songhai

bio.en: Ruler who made Songhai the largest empire in West African history, with Timbuktu flourishing as a centre of learning.

role.en: sultan who took in the Jews expelled from Spain

bio.en: Son of Mehmed II, he spent years countering the claims of his brother Cem; in 1492 he welcomed the Sephardic Jews expelled from Spain. He was deposed by his own son Selim.

role.en: navigator

bio.en: Genoese navigator in Spanish service who reached the Americas in 1492, opening them to Europe.

role.en: Queen of Castile

bio.en: With her husband Ferdinand she united Spain, completed the Reconquista and sponsored Columbus's voyage.

role.en: painter, scientist and inventor

bio.en: Universal genius of the Renaissance who painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper; his notebooks brim with inventions.

role.en: last Plantagenet king, killed at Bosworth

bio.en: Brother of Edward IV who took the throne from his young nephew; the 'Princes in the Tower' vanished. He died at the Battle of Bosworth in 1485, the last English king killed in battle; his remains were found under a Leicester car park in 2012.

role.en: navigator

bio.en: A Florentine in Spanish and Portuguese service who sailed along South America and was among the first to see it as a new continent rather than Asia. In 1507 the cartographer Waldseemüller named the New World America after him.

role.en: Grand Princess of Moscow

bio.en: Niece of the last Byzantine emperor and wife of Ivan III, linked to Moscow's adoption of Byzantine imperial symbols.

role.en: founder of the Tudor dynasty who ended the Wars of the Roses

bio.en: He defeated Richard III at Bosworth and, by marrying Elizabeth of York, united the red and white roses. He founded the Tudor dynasty, filled the treasury and tamed the rebellious nobility.

role.en: "the Last Knight", who raised the Habsburgs through shrewd marriages

bio.en: His marriage to Mary of Burgundy brought him the Netherlands, and the marriages of his children and grandchildren brought Spain, Bohemia and Hungary. He carried out the Imperial Reform of 1495 and in 1508 took the title "Elected Roman Emperor" without a papal coronation.

role.en: the "Father of the People" who fought for Milan

bio.en: The only king from the Orléans branch of the Valois. He continued the Italian Wars and seized the Duchy of Milan, and tax cuts earned him the name "Father of the People".

role.en: Sapa Inca

bio.en: Under him the Inca Empire reached its greatest extent; his death from smallpox triggered a civil war.

role.en: shogun whose birth set off the Ōnin War

bio.en: Yoshimasa's son, whose birth in 1465 displaced his uncle Yoshimi as heir and led to the Ōnin War. Shogun from 1473, he tried to reassert control over the provinces and died in 1489 on campaign against the Rokkaku in Ōmi.

role.en: Aztec emperor

bio.en: Ruler of the Aztecs at their zenith who met Cortés's conquistadors and died as their captive.

role.en: shogun who held office twice and was driven out twice

bio.en: Shogun 1490–1493, deposed in Hosokawa Masamoto's coup (the Meiō Incident). In 1508 he returned with Ōuchi Yoshioki's army and ruled again until 1521, when he fled Hosokawa Takakuni; he died in exile on Awaji.

role.en: Dutch humanist

bio.en: The best-known scholar of the Northern Renaissance. He published the Greek New Testament (1516) and mocked the failings of clergy and scholars in The Praise of Folly.

role.en: founder of Sikhism

bio.en: First Sikh Guru, who preached the oneness of God, human equality and rejection of caste.

role.en: navigator

bio.en: Portuguese navigator who first sailed from Europe around Africa to India in 1498.

role.en: Florentine political thinker and diplomat

bio.en: In The Prince he separated politics from morality, judging a ruler by whether he keeps power and the state. The word "Machiavellian" comes from his name.

role.en: king who started the Italian Wars

bio.en: In 1494–1495 he marched the length of Italy and took Naples but was forced to retreat. He died aged 27 after striking his head on a door lintel at the château of Amboise.

role.en: sultan who took Cairo and Mecca

bio.en: He deposed his father, defeated Shah Ismail at Chaldiran in 1514 and in 1516–1517 destroyed the Mamluk Sultanate, annexing Syria, Egypt and the Hejaz; in eight years he nearly doubled the empire.

role.en: Chinese Neo-Confucian philosopher

bio.en: Taught that the principle of things lies within one's own heart-mind and that knowledge and action are one: to know the good and not do it is not to know it. Also a senior official and general.

role.en: astronomer

bio.en: Proposed the heliocentric model, placing the Sun rather than the Earth at the centre of the universe.

role.en: sculptor, painter and architect

bio.en: Titan of the Renaissance who created David, the Sistine Chapel frescoes and the dome of St Peter's.

role.en: grand prince who completed the unification of the Russian lands

bio.en: Son of Ivan III and Sophia Palaiologina and father of Ivan the Terrible. He annexed Pskov (1510), Smolensk (1514) and Ryazan (1521), completing the gathering of the lands of north-eastern Rus.

role.en: navigator

bio.en: Led the first circumnavigation of the globe, finding the strait into the Pacific, but was killed in the Philippines.

role.en: puppet shogun of the Hosokawa clan

bio.en: Installed in 1494 by Hosokawa Masamoto after Yoshitane's overthrow, he ruled only in Masamoto's name. Left without support when Masamoto was murdered in 1507, he fled Kyoto in 1508 and died in exile in Ōmi.

role.en: founder of the Mughal Empire

bio.en: Descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan who won at Panipat and founded the Mughal Empire; author of the memoir Baburnama.

role.en: church reformer

bio.en: The monk whose 95 Theses of 1517 launched the Protestant Reformation; he translated the Bible into German.

role.en: friar and defender of Native Americans

bio.en: A former colonist turned friar who spent his life denouncing the brutality of the conquest; his Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies was read across Europe.

role.en: conquistador

bio.en: Spanish conquistador who, with a small force and Indigenous allies, overthrew the Aztec Empire.

role.en: Bengali saint, founder of Gaudiya Vaishnavism

bio.en: Preached love for Krishna through the communal chanting of his names, kirtan, open to people of every caste. He spent his last years in Puri. The Hare Krishna movement traces its teaching back to him.

role.en: printer and humanist

bio.en: A native of Polotsk and a Padua doctor of medicine. In 1517 in Prague he began printing the Bible in the Ruthenian recension of Church Slavonic, the first printed book of the Eastern Slavs, and later set up a press in Vilnius.

role.en: king of six wives who broke with Rome and created the Church of England

bio.en: To divorce Catherine of Aragon he broke with the pope, declared himself head of the Church of England in 1534 and then dissolved the monasteries. He married six times; two of his wives, Anne Boleyn and Catherine Howard, were beheaded.

role.en: Ottoman sultan

bio.en: Sultan under whom the Ottoman Empire reached its peak; at home he was called Kanuni, 'the Lawgiver'.

role.en: Renaissance king who brought Leonardo to France

bio.en: He won at Marignano (1515) but was captured by Charles V at Pavia in 1525. Patron of Leonardo da Vinci, he built Chambord and made French the language of official acts by the Ordinance of Villers-Cotterêts.

role.en: mystic poet

bio.en: Rajput princess who renounced court life for devotion to Krishna; her bhajans are still sung across India.
